issues.description: SealSaloon.orders attribute: The problem statement requires a modifiable List<Meal> called `orders` (problem_statement.md says `List<Meal>`), but the provided solution implements `orders` as a Meal[] array (solution SealSaloon.java declares `private Meal[] orders;`). The template also provides ArrayHelpers that operate on arrays (template ArrayHelpers.addElementToArray), which encourages using arrays instead of List. This mismatch between the specified type (List) and the actual/template code (array) can confuse students about which collection type and API to use and whether tests or the UML expect a List or an array.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification and template/solution consistent. Either: (A) Update the problem statement and UML to permit using arrays (explain that a modifiable collection may be an array) and keep ArrayHelpers and the solution as-is; or (B) Change the template and reference solution to use a modifiable List<Meal> (e.g., private List<Meal> orders = new ArrayList<>();) and replace/augment ArrayHelpers with List-based utilities (or remove it). Ensure the UML, examples, and all descriptions consistently refer to the chosen collection type (List or array) and update code samples and tests accordingly.
